title: How to Shop Online Safely in Pakistan — 6 Rules That Prevent 99% of Scams
author: Omar Farooq
authorBio: Founder of BazaarNow. Has been buying and selling online in Pakistan since 2022. Has been scammed exactly twice. Both times ignored his own rules. Wrote this post so you don't have to learn the hard way.
excerpt: Online shopping in Pakistan is growing 35% every year — and so are the scams. Six rules to shop safely, spot fake stores, and never lose money to a WhatsApp DP that vanishes.

sections.content: Pakistan's e-commerce market grew 35% last year. So did the number of fake Instagram stores with zero inventory, stolen product photos, and a WhatsApp number that stops replying the moment you send money. The scams are not getting more sophisticated. They're the same three tricks, recycled endlessly, because they keep working. This post is the antidote. Six rules. None of them complicated. All of them learned the expensive way — sometimes by me, sometimes by customers who told me their stories while placing their first COD order with shaking hands. Figuratively shaking. Probably literally shaking too. Getting scammed feels personal. It is personal. Someone took your money and gave you nothing. Let's make sure it doesn't happen again.

sections.title: The Six Rules (Read This If You Read Nothing Else)
items: Never pay in advance to a store you haven't ordered from at least twice before — COD is your shield
A real store has a physical address, a landline or business WhatsApp, and at least 30 days of visible social media history
If the price is 50% below every other listing, the product does not exist — you're about to fund someone's dinner, not receive a package
Check the product images: reverse-search them on Google Images. If they appear on 14 other sites with different prices, none of those stores have the product
A store that pressures you to 'order now, only 2 left' is using urgency to bypass your judgment — walk away
Save every screenshot: order confirmation, payment receipt, chat history. If something goes wrong, these are your evidence

sections.text: Rule 1: If a store won't offer COD, there's a reason — and the reason is never good

sections.content: We wrote a [whole post about COD in Pakistan](/blog/cash-on-delivery-pakistan-online-shopping). Here's the safety-specific version: cash on delivery is the only payment method where the risk sits with the seller, not the buyer. You inspect the product. You pay. If the box contains a brick, you don't pay. This is not complicated. Any store that refuses COD on first orders is asking you to trust them with zero evidence. Some legitimate stores do this because COD returns cost them money. Fair. But you're not obligated to be their first test case. Order COD. Build trust. Switch to advance payment later for the 5% discount. That's the sequence. COD first, discount second. Never the other way around.

sections.text: Rule 2: A real store exists somewhere you can visit — even if you never will

sections.content: Every legitimate online store in Pakistan has a physical presence. A warehouse. An office. A shop in a commercial area. Even if 100% of their sales happen online, the stock lives somewhere. Ask yourself: if I demanded to pick up my order in person, could I? If the answer is no — if the store is 'online only' with no address, no location, no 'come see us' — that's not a store. That's a guy with a phone and stolen photos.

At BazaarNow, our address is on the [contact page](/contact). We don't expect you to visit. (It's not a showroom. It's where we pack orders. You'd be bored.) But the fact that the address exists, that you could stand outside it, that a human answers the phone there — that's the signal. Not the address itself. The existence of one.

sections.text: Rule 3: The price is the tell — too cheap means too fake

sections.content: Genuine AirPods Pro cost Rs. 55,000 in Pakistan. Not Rs. 55,000 'approximately.' Exactly Rs. 54,999 at authorised retailers. If you see 'Original AirPods Pro — Rs. 3,500' with free delivery, what you're buying is a pair of plastic earpieces that will connect to your phone for exactly 17 minutes before emitting a sound best described as 'my battery is dying and also I am not a real AirPod.'

The rule of thumb: if a price is more than 40% below the market average for that product, you are not getting a deal. You are getting scammed. The 'deal' is imaginary. The loss is real. There is no wholesaler in Sialkot selling genuine Apple products at 90% off. If there were, they wouldn't be advertising on Instagram Stories. They'd be on the front page of the Wall Street Journal.

sections.text: Rule 4: Reverse-search the product photos — it takes 30 seconds and reveals everything

sections.content: Right-click any product photo. Select 'Search image with Google.' If the same image appears on AliExpress, Daraz, five Instagram stores, and a Shopify site with a domain registered last Tuesday — none of those sellers have the actual product. They all have the same photo. At best, one of them might dropship it. At worst, none of them have anything and they're all using the same stolen image. Either way, you shouldn't be the one figuring out which is which with your own money.

BazaarNow uses product images from our suppliers and partners. They're not stock photos. They're not 'representative images.' They're the actual product in someone's actual warehouse, photographed under lighting that is sometimes unflattering and occasionally features someone's thumb in the corner. We keep the thumb photos. They're honest.

sections.text: Rule 5: Urgency is manipulation — 'only 2 left' means 'don't think, just pay'

sections.content: Scarcity is real in e-commerce. Sometimes a product genuinely has limited stock. But when every product on a store shows 'Only 3 left — order now!' — that's not inventory management. That's a countdown timer designed by someone who read a blog post about conversion rate optimization in 2019 and made it their entire personality.

A legitimate store tells you when something is genuinely low in stock — and lets you decide. BazaarNow shows stock counts when they're low (under 10 units). We don't put fake countdowns on 1,800 products. We're too lazy to maintain that. Also, it's dishonest. Mostly the second thing. But the laziness helps.

sections.text: Rule 6: Screenshot everything — your phone's gallery is your insurance policy

sections.content: Before you pay: screenshot the product page. Screenshot the price. Screenshot your order confirmation. Screenshot the chat where the seller confirmed the delivery time. If everything goes well — and 95% of the time it will — you'll never need these. If something goes wrong, you have timestamped evidence of exactly what was promised. This turns a 'he said, she said' into 'here's what he said, here's the screenshot, please process my refund.' Banks and payment processors love screenshots. They're the closest thing to a witness in an online transaction.

sections.text: Don't shop online in Pakistan if…

sections.content: You're the type of person who sees a 'too good to be true' price and thinks 'but what if it IS true.' It's not. This is not a movie. There's no montage where the underdog finds a secret supplier and everyone lives happily ever after. You will lose money. You will feel stupid. Buy from stores with real addresses, real phone numbers, and prices that make mathematical sense. The deal you're looking for is not the 90%-off unicorn. It's the 5% advance payment discount on a store you already trust. That's real. That's repeatable. That won't make you feel foolish on a Tuesday afternoon.

Also: don't shop online if you're in a rush and can't wait 2-4 working days. Impatience leads to bad decisions. You'll order from the first store that promises 'same-day delivery' without checking if they're legitimate. Go to the physical market if you need it today. Come back to us when you can wait a few days. We'll be here, with real products, real prices, and no countdown timers. (Except the 5% discount. That one's real. But it doesn't expire. It's been 5% since we launched. It'll be 5% next year. No urgency. Just math.)

sections.text: Straight answers to the safety questions everyone asks

items.q: How do I know if an online store in Pakistan is genuine?
items.a: Check four things: a physical address listed on the site, a working phone number or WhatsApp, at least 30 days of visible social media posts, and real product photos (not stock images). All four present? Likely genuine. Two or fewer? Proceed with COD only, or not at all.

items.q: What should I do if I get scammed by an online store?
items.a: If you paid via bank transfer, contact your bank immediately with screenshots. If via JazzCash or EasyPaisa, report the transaction in the app. For COD scams (product not as described), refuse delivery. For advance payment scams, file a complaint with the FIA Cyber Crime Wing at [nr3c.gov.pk](https://nr3c.gov.pk). The more evidence you have (screenshots, chat logs), the better your chances.

COD protects you from losing money on a product that never arrives or is fake. It doesn't protect you from inconvenience. Always open and inspect the package before paying. If the rider pressures you to pay first, stand firm. It's your right. Read our [full COD guide](/blog/cash-on-delivery-pakistan-online-shopping) for the detailed walkthrough.

items.q: Are Instagram and Facebook stores safe to buy from?
items.a: Some are. Many aren't. The platform doesn't vet sellers. Check if they have a website, a physical address, and customer reviews on Google (not just their own page). An Instagram page with 50,000 followers and no website is still just an Instagram page. Followers can be bought. A website with a real domain and an SSL certificate is harder to fake.

items.q: What's the safest way to pay for online shopping?
items.a: COD for first orders — always. Once you trust a store, advance payment via JazzCash or EasyPaisa is safe and gets you discounts. Never send money via personal bank transfer to an individual's account unless you've verified the store extensively. Read our [JazzCash payment guide](/blog/how-to-pay-with-jazzcash-online-pakistan) for more.

We guarantee that if you receive a damaged or misrepresented product, we'll refund you — full amount, no store credit, no arguments. Our [return policy](/returns) covers 7 days from delivery. We also don't hold inventory — we arrange products through partners. The small print on the checkout page says exactly this. We're not hiding anything. Read it. It's actually there.

sections.content: Online shopping in Pakistan is safe when you follow the rules. COD first. Check the address. Reverse-search the photos. Screenshot everything. If a deal feels too good to be true, close the tab. The money you save by not getting scammed is worth more than any discount a fake store is offering. And when you're ready to shop somewhere that follows its own rules — BazaarNow is at [bazaarnow.net](https://www.bazaarnow.net). 1,964 products. Free delivery. 5% off on advance payment. And zero countdown timers. (Except this post. You've been reading for 7 minutes. That's probably long enough. Go outside. Touch grass. Then come back and shop.)
